chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: Wanderlust at the railroad station
summary: Watching the trains and ships made him long to go away.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah,, this is somethin'. You got all these railroads here. You got to see these big engines on those railroads. See people going away when you're by the railroad station. You'd long to go away yourself. "Some day I'll get a chance to go away. Maybe I'll get a chance to get on that ship and go somewhere." You're young and you've got this wanderlust. You want to go somewhere. You want to see things.
They got these trains... The L&M Railroad was about four blocks from my house. I'd see this fast train leave

out in the morning, come back in. Jeff...what do you call it, Jeff Holloway. Do you remember that? The L&M Indian out there? And you'd go up to the IC, and you'd see the station, people...people well-dressed... You'd see people happy and well-dressed, not people sad, going to some towns in Georgia and Mississippi, the little small towns. And you'd see everybody relaxed, you know.
